subject: Latency funnel & deployment decision log (post-call)
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com

Subject: Post-call — latency/throughput summary & options

Hi Sienna / Dirk —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Short recap from our discovery call and the concrete options we discussed so the execs at LenvioTech have a clean decision log. TL;DR: LenvioTech needs tight 95th/99th latency SLOs for live credit-checks while handling spikes from marketing campaigns (bursty QPS), and prefers a predictable cost envelope for procurement.

Key pain points we captured:
- P1: 95th percentile tail latency impacting user flow (~150–200ms target for inference).
- P2: Peak bursts during campaign windows (10–20x baseline QPS for 10–30 mins).
- P3: Procurement requires an explicit capacity/cost playbook and an operations runbook for audits.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce user-facing inference latency to <=150ms p95 for the credit-check path; p99 target <=350ms.
- Handle sustained baseline of ~120 QPS with capacity to burst to ~1500 QPS for short windows without degraded p95 for high-priority traffic.
- SLA language that ties latency buckets to credits and specifies fallback behaviour.

Technical notes and options we discussed:
1) Deployment topology choices
   - Hosted (fastest): Redwood-hosted API with reserved capacity for the peak windows + autoscale buffer. Good for quick time to value and simpler procurement.
   - Dedicated pool: Reserved GPU pool (private customer tenancy) with capacity planning that matches baseline + burst runway. Predictable, fits procurement, supports model variants and kv-cache across nodes.
   - Private (VPC): Customer-managed VPC with dedicated control plane — best for data residency/audit needs but longer lead time.

2) Model and runtime guidance (initial recommendation)
   - Candidate model: Llama-3-8B (quantized FP16/8-bit) for the credit-check path — balance of latency and quality.
   - KV cache + prefix caching for session reuse (significant p95 improvements for multi-turn checks).
   - Aggressive batching for background/rerank paths; real-time path should use micro-batching (batch size 1–4) to meet p95.

3) SLO & routing strategy
   - Priority routing: Route critical credit-check requests to a low-latency pool (reserved nodes) while best-effort flows go to cost-optimized nodes.
   - Canary & fallback: Canary new model versions to 5% traffic, automatic fallback to previous variant on p99 regressions.

Action items we promised today:
- Redwood: share a one-page ops & SLA draft + topology diagram (attached) — Markus (this thread).
- Redwood: high-level cost snapshot for Dedicated vs Hosted with burst assumptions — Jordan.
- LenvioTech: confirm whether data residency requires VPC/on-prem (affects timeline).
- LenvioTech procurement: point of contact and any preferred contract cycle (monthly/annual).

Attachments: lenviotech-ops-sla-draft.pdf (proposal), redwood-topology-options.png (diagram)

Next proposed touchpoints:
- Internal: Redwood alignment meeting (Markus / Irene / Jordan) — Wed 2026-05-21
- Follow-up call with LenvioTech to review SLAs and cost snapshot — Fri 2026-05-22 (proposed)

Thanks — Ireneg if you have technical additions feel free to append.

Thanks Markus — this is very helpful and captures the call well. A couple clarifications / asks from our side: 

1) The p95 target of <=150ms is for the full end-to-end credit decision (including pre/post processing). For planning, assume ~40ms budget for network + preproc, so inference p95 should target <=110ms.
2) For bursts: the 10–20x number is correct. Typical baseline is ~120 QPS during working hours; marketing blasts can push to ~2k QPS for ~15 minutes.

Can you also call out:
- Expected cold-start behaviour for dedicated pools during the first 15 minutes of a burst.
- Any quantization or model-change risk to accuracy; we need to present an accuracy delta to compliance (we track false-positive rate tightly).

Procurement is on cc — they'd like a draft T&Cs timeline and a ballpark of committed monthly spend for Dedicated with a burst buffer. If you can get the high-level cost snapshot by Fri that would be ideal.

Also, small ask: can you include a short simulation of p95 under 5 deployment topologies (hosted small, hosted reserved, dedicated small, dedicated large, private) — just QPS vs expected p95 numbers? That will help our architecture committee choose.

Appreciate it,
Sienna
VP Product, LenvioTech

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Post-call — latency/throughput summary & options (technical addendum)

Hi Sienna / Markus — adding the technical deep-dive and a simple model-fit note. I included a small table in the attached PDF; pasted the short version here.

Model & latency expectations (baseline config, NVLink-enabled GPUs, quantized 8-bit runtimes):
- Llama-3-8B (int8): single-token decode latency ~6–9ms on A10-like instance; end-to-end (micro-batch 1, softmax) inference p95 ~60–90ms depending on sequence length (credit-checks typically ~60–80 tokens).
- Llama-3-13B (quant8): single-token ~9–14ms; p95 ~120–180ms. Higher quality but costlier and risk to p95 during bursts.

KV cache / prefix caching notes:
- For session-based checks where multiple calls reuse context, KV cache reduces p95 by ~30–50% for subsequent calls. We'll instrument to route cache-hits to warm pools.

Burst handling & cold-starts:
- Dedicated reserved pools: warm nodes can absorb short bursts without cold-start penalty if core is kept warm (small keep-alive). If burst > warm capacity, autoscale steps will add nodes — expect 20–90s scale-up depending on quota and GPU spin-up; we recommend a small reserved burst buffer to meet p95 during 15-min blasts.
- Hosted with burst reservations: generally faster spin-up but shared tenancy means less deterministic p95 at the tail.

Accuracy/quantization guidance:
- We will run a small eval pack (10k prompts from your historical log) comparing FP16 vs int8 quantized variants and produce delta metrics (accuracy, false-positive rate). Typical delta for 8-bit on 8B models is <1.5% across decision labels for tuned evals, but we'll confirm.

Attached: lenviotech-ops-sla-draft.pdf (ops + one-pager), redwood-topology-options.png (simple topology sketches), eval-plan.md (evaluation steps) — eval-plan.md is inline in the Drive link.

I can run the 5-topology p95 simulation Sienna requested — Jordan, can you take the cost snapshots and simulated p95s by Friday? I'll coordinate the eval.

--
